# service-compris

> A Firebase backend you **install libraries onto** rather than deploy features into.
> A JSON manifest becomes collections, schemas and access rules on a running host —
> no function deployment, no code review, no redeploy. Agents authenticate with
> scoped tokens that attenuate their human's authority and die when it does.

Status: **0.2.0-beta.2**, 2026-09-21. beta.1 was cut to be broken; the first
consumer broke it within a day and filed eight issues, all now closed. Verified
against a real deployed host on every change — 94 assertions across six
ceremonies (`scripts/verify-*.js`).

## Start here

- [BETA.md](BETA.md): the walkthrough — stand up a host, claim it, write a manifest,
  install it, give an agent an identity. Also lists what is deliberately not ready.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed and, for each fix, what the bug actually was.
- [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md): dated, append-only architectural decisions. Read before
  proposing changes to RBAC, the access model, or the endpoint surface — several of
  those questions are settled and the reasoning matters more than the conclusion.

## The seven things that will save you the most time

1. **A `404` usually means "not allowed", not "not there".** Denials are opaque to
   non-privileged callers on purpose — a protected document and a missing one must be
   indistinguishable, or the status code enumerates what exists. Only
   `admin`/`developer`/`owner` see the real `403`.
2. **Collections must be namespaced**: `yourlib:thing`. A bare name is the platform's,
   always. The separator is `:` — `/` already separates sub-collections.
3. **Mutating requests put the path in the BODY.** `GET`/`DELETE` use `?p=`;
   `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` send `{"p": "...", "data": {...}}`. `POST /docs
   {writes:[…]}` commits several documents atomically.
4. **`access` is an array, not a role-keyed object.** Grants join as a lattice, so
   order is meaningless and holding more roles never grants less.
5. **A fresh function may answer `401` with HTML from *Google*, not from us.** It needs
   an `allUsers` run.invoker binding. Ours carry CORS and rate-limit headers; that is
   the tell. `provision-sandbox.js` grants them.
6. **Errors are `{error: "<code>", message, details?}`.** Switch on the code; the
   prose is free to change. Opaque `404`s carry no detail, by design.
7. **Endpoint-managed fields are hidden from your schema** — `_created`,
   `_modified`, `_seq`, `_by` — so `additionalProperties: false` works.

## Endpoints

- `/doc` — single document CRUD. `GET`/`DELETE` take `?p=collection/id`;
  `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` take `{p, data}` in the body. `?p=coll/field=value` resolves
  by a field in `unique` or `tagFields`.
- `/docs` — collection queries (`?p=`, `c=` limit, `f=` fields, `o=` order), the
  delta cursor (`since=<seq>` → `{rows, cursor, more}`), and `POST {writes:[…]}`
  for an atomic multi-document commit.
- `/install` — `POST {manifest, approving?}` installs or upgrades; `GET` lists;
  `DELETE ?name=` revokes. Requires `configurator`, and specifically **not** `owner`.
  `GET ?name=<ns>` answers `{name, version, status}` to any authenticated
  principal, tokens included.
- `/claim` — `GET` publishes a nonce; write it into the datastore by hand to prove
  ownership, then `POST` (authenticated) to mint the first `configurator`.
- `/token` — `POST` mints a scoped token, `GET` lists your own, `DELETE ?id=` revokes.
- `/authorize` — the browser loop that gives a CLI its first token.
  `?action=start|approve|exchange|config`; `GET ?request=<id>` is the consent page.
- `/esm`, `/stored`, `/gen`, `/prefetch`, `/cachedQuery`, `/user`, `/sitemap` — the
  older surface. See `docs/`, but trust the code over the file paths in it: they
  predate the `collections/` reorganisation.

## Rules a manifest lives by

- **Upgrades are additive-only.** Removing a collection or field, newly *requiring* a
  field, or changing a unique constraint are refused as migrations rather than
  guessed at. A newly-required field would invalidate every stored document.
- **A published version's content is immutable.** Re-POSTing the same version is
  normal; re-POSTing different content under the same version is a `409`.
- **Revoking never drops rows.** Collections become unreachable; documents stay.
- **v1 is declarative only.** A `functions` key is a hard failure, not an ignored
  field. Stored ajs is install v2.
- **`envelope: { seq: true }`** assigns a monotonic `_seq` so a replica can resume.
  Opt-in: a total order serialises writes to that collection at roughly one per
  second, through one counter document. **`requireAttribution: true`** refuses a
  write the endpoint cannot attribute.
  **Declare `seq` before the first write:** an upgrade that turns it on or off
  for an existing collection is refused, because earlier (or later) documents
  would carry no `_seq` and be invisible to `since=`.
- **`immutable: true`** (top level of a collection, beside `schema`) makes a
  stored document unchangeable: an identical re-write is a no-op, a different one
  is refused with `409 {error: "immutable"}` — in a batch, the whole commit is.
  Deletes are refused too, and an upgrade may add it but never drop it. Without it an upsert over an existing id REPLACES it
  and assigns a new `_seq`. Declare it on any log you replicate.
- **A role pre-assigned by contact email resolves only for a VERIFIED email.**
  Password sign-up is enabled on provisioned hosts, so an unverified address is
  a claim anyone can make.
- **The `system` namespace is the platform's.** A manifest named `system`, or
  declaring `system:*`, is refused.
- **Capabilities are shape-only so far.** The format is settled and validated, but
  nothing consults `grant.capabilities` yet. The install response reports
  `unenforced: [...]` so you are never told you hold a power you do not.

## What a token is

`(principal, caveats)`. Effective authority is recomputed **on every request** as
`rolesOf(principal) ∩ caveats.roles`. So a token never holds what its principal does
not hold right now, and revoking a human revokes every agent they authorised —
instantly, with no revocation list. `owner`, `configurator` and `developer` can never
be carried by one. A token cannot mint another. `DELETE` is not a default method. The
secret is shown once and never stored, only hashed.

## Repository shape

- `functions/src/collections/` — the portable decision kernel. No Firebase imports;
  this is what the `service-compris` npm package publishes.
- `functions/src/install/`, `functions/src/auth/` — install and auth, each split into
  pure decisions plus a thin HTTP handler. If it is a judgement, it belongs in the
  pure half where it runs without a cloud.
- `scripts/verify-*.js` — acceptance against a LIVE host, six ceremonies:
  install, token, authorize, sequence, batch, provenance. `--alias <name>`
  targets a project. Run these first on a new host; if they pass, anything you
  hit afterwards is your manifest or our design, not a broken deploy.
- `src/` — client code, which is **leaving**. Do not build on it; see ROADMAP.md.

## Where to push hardest

The manifest format. It was designed against three consumers and validated against
one. If it cannot express something your design needs, **that is the bug** — say so
rather than bending your design around it. A weakness found now is an issue comment;
the same weakness after adoption is a migration.

Issues: https://github.com/tonioloewald/tosijs-platform/issues
